sub.en: Look at the questions. What comes after the question word — the person, or do/does?

items.q: Where ___ you live?
items.why: question word + do/does + person + verb. The verb keeps its base form.

items.q: What time ___ she start work?

Who ___ you work with?
Why ___ he want to learn English?
How long ___ your meetings usually last?
Where ___ you go on holiday last year?
items.why: RECYCLED: the same shape in the past — did + base form.

acts.title: Checking you understood
text: A: So, tell me about your day. What time do you start?
B: Half past seven. — A: Sorry, can you repeat that? — B: Half past seven.
A: And who do you work with? — B: A team of six people. — A: Do you mean six, or sixteen? — B: Six.
A: So you start at half past seven and you work in a team of six. Is that right?
B: That’s right. And I finish at four, because I start early.

items.s: B starts work at half past seven.
A asks B to repeat the time.
B works in a team of sixteen.
A checks the information at the end.
B finishes early because he starts early.

write.q: Write eight questions for an interview about someone’s job. Use where, what, what time, when, why, who, how long and how often — one question for each.
write.model: Where do you work? What do you do there? What time do you start? When do you take a break? Why do you like your job? Who do you work with? How long do you work every day? How often do you have meetings?

speak.q: Interview a partner out loud with five wh- questions. Check one answer with “Sorry, can you repeat that?” and one with “So you…?”
speak.model: Where do you work? How often do you travel for work? — Sorry, can you repeat that? — So you travel once a month and you work from home the rest of the time?
